scope: Proposition 5.9 of the manuscript “A hyperbolic group with no geometric CAT(0) action” (preprints/A-hyperbolic-group-with-no-geometric-CAT0-action-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 257 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 124f55b0821cc7f1), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 32-33. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let Pν be a sequence of aspherical instances whose master-match statistics and six-letter relative counts satisfy the conclusions of Proposition 4.5, with errors tending to zero for every fixed test and every fixed t. If every π1(Pν) has a proper cocompact isometric action on a proper complete CAT(0) space, then there are a complete CAT(0) space Z, a configuration indexed by the core vertices of Γ, and a point c ∈ Z with the following properties. 1. Every core edge has length one. Every nonbacktracking two-edge core path has squared endpoint distance two. Every three-edge core path with distinct admissible fields has squared endpoint distance at least three. 32 2. Every core hexagon has its three opposite-pair midpoints equal to c. All core vertices have distance r = √ 3/2 from c. For any two vertices occurring in one core hexagon, their central triangle with c is flat and their tangent scalar product is given by Equation (5.15). 3. With H0 = CD and J = mid(XC, YC), one has d(H0, J)2 = 1 2 , d(H0, XD) = 1, ∠H0 (J, XD) ≥ π 2 . More precisely, all the fractional-point inequalities in Equation (5.18) hold.
